reasons.claim: Ramaria safraniolens (VU, forest-associated, site-bound fungus; threats include lack of continuity forest, lack of large/old trees, soil disturbance in forestry) recorded 229 m from the polygon edge in 2023, 10 m uncertainty. This is an eligible species within 250 m, so the rubric gives HIGH.
Three more eligible species lie beyond 250 m within 1000 m: Alectoria sarmentosa (VU, 721 m), Goodyera repens (VU, 745 m), Phellopilus nigrolimitatus (VU, 833 m).

Site-bound forest NT fungi recorded within 250 m: Fomitopsis rosea (120 m), Phellinidium ferrugineofuscum (120 m), Hermanssonia centrifuga (130 m). Five site-bound forest NT species within 1000 m in total.
No completed felling overlaps the 0.97 ha polygon. Effort is adequate (72nd percentile, 11 records within 250 m).

uncertainties: Records are from 2023 and outside the polygon (none inside); presence on the site now is not shown.
The polygon is small (0.97 ha, equivalent radius 55 m); the 229 m record is well beyond the site's own scale.
Effort comparison relies on a county sample from a short window.
not_established: That Ramaria safraniolens or any other species occupies the polygon.
Absence of records inside the polygon does not mean absence of species.
Nothing here says the site is safe to fell or that felling is unlawful.
next_action: Reviewer should check where the 2023 Ramaria safraniolens record and nearby NT fungi lie relative to the polygon, and inspect the stand for continuity-forest and old-tree features before felling begins.
